title: Charles Hunt receives award for best publication on effective lawmaking
text:
Charles Hunt receives award for best publication on effective lawmaking
Charles Hunt, an associate professor of political science, was honored with an award from the Center for Effective Lawmaking at their annual conference, according to a July 8 announcement. Hunt received recognition for the best publication on effective lawmaking published in the previous calendar year.
The award-winning article, co-authored by Hunt and Kristina C. Miller of the University of Maryland, is titled “How Modern Lawmakers Advertise Their Legislative Effectiveness to Constituents.”
Hunt’s research explores how lawmakers communicate their legislative effectiveness to constituents. The Center for Effective Lawmaking presents this annual award to recognize outstanding scholarship that advances understanding of legislative processes and outcomes.
Hunt holds a Ph.D. and serves as an associate professor at Boise State University.
